rule:
- Cutting immediately AFTER a function word (an article, preposition, conjunction, auxiliary or
  determiner: the, a, an, of, to, in, on, at, for, with, from, by, and, or, but, is, are, was,
  were, be, been, that, which, as, its, their, this, these, than, into) LOOKS wrong because the
  left side ends on a word that expects a continuation. Measurement says otherwise: these
  positions are consistently scored TOO LOW relative to what they measure. Do not penalise a
  position merely because the left side ends on such a word — score it on what the remainder
  could overturn, not on whether the left side reads as finished.
